text_fidelity_a:
Flambeau Outdoors Tactical Personal Defense Weapon (PDW) Case, Portable Firearm Storage Accessory We have been using the heavy-duty Pelican cases for years with the long guns and for good reasons, so I was quite interested to see this case from Flambeau. My primary question was if the construction quality was comparable with Pelican since the two are priced similarly.

This one is marketed as extra large and they aren't joking - see my photos. I have placed two shotguns and a rifle (all with different barrel lengths) in the case for comparison purposes to show the size. And of course the two handguns for scale. You can absolutely carry scoped rifles without trouble or damage in this case. There are three layers of foam, including a pick and pull customizable layer.

It's a good thing this has two handles and wheels because empty, this case weighs at least 20lbs. Once you've packed it for a hunting trip or a run to the skeet range, it's not like grabbing that generic, fabric rifle case you used to use. This is the big leagues. The wheels seem pretty sturdy and roll smoothly on tile and cement, but they aren't meant for dirt. How they will perform long term remains to be seen.

I do like that Flambeau took a page from the Pelican book and has reinforced the plastic hinges with steel. See the photo. The hinges are the natural weak point, so this should help increase longevity. The hinges do move smoothly and without hanging up. There are two stainless locking connections for padlocks - always a good idea whether you fly or not.

I hauled this monster out to the farm yesterday with the Remington 870 for a bit of target practice. I threw it in the back of the truck and went. My husband's shotgun was just as pristine when I got there as it was before I left. (Whew) The case had no damage other than some hay and dirt on the outside - none got inside. I'm going to look and see what this company makes for a single handgun.
text_fidelity_b: Flambeau Outdoors Tactical Personal Defense Weapon (PDW) Case, Portable Firearm Storage Accessory

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) Needs an indicator on the device for battery life. Definitely get a screen protector, otherwise it will get very shallow scratches that deter from the nice looking screen. I have it connected to bluetooth for constant syncing/updating of information, so the battery life isn't that great - typically 2 days.
I've not had the rash problem I've read about others having. The purple is nice an compliments much of my purple oriented wardrobe.

The combination of the watch and the software make this a great motivator. The software/app could do for some improvements - logging food is a chore - but I love the competitions and the ability to quickly check my status for steps or other on the fly. I would NOT want one without the screen. The hear rate monitor seems pretty accurate for me. I've compared the results to using an oximeter and the hand holds on my elliptical machine and they are all +/-2 or 3 BPM. A nurse was measuring my hear rate a couple weeks ago and she was way off.
I do with that while you're in exercise mode you could cycle through to see daily totals as well. I sometimes will extend my run to meet daily goals and if all I can see is my workout steps/cals/floors/etc, I'm having to work on memory or blindly.

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I have been wanting a Fitbit for a really long time.  I did some research because I was not sure which one I wanted.  I went to the website and read about them all.  This one had all the features that I wanted.  I never wear a watch and my cell phone is too big to fit in my pocket while I work out.  So it was important for me that I could view time with my Fitbit.  Just a tap of the screen and I can view the time.  Or I can just flick my wrist and the time displays.  Or I can press the button on the side.  The Fitbit HR is thicker than what I would have liked, but it is not worth giving it less than 5 stars over that.  I can view my steps and check my heart rate.  Many reviews have said that the heart rate is not accurate.  Honestly that is not a feature that was a make it or break it to me.  I don't know if the heart rate is accurate or not.  The Fitbit also lets me know how many miles I have walked. It also tracks if I went up any flights of steps or not. I can even use it as an alarm.  It just vibrates gently.  Setting up the Fitbit and syncing it to my Android phone was a breeze.  The app is great.  The Fitbit HR also tracks my sleep patterns.  I can set challenges for myself and even challenge others.  The first day I set up a challenge to take 10,000 steps.  Throughout the day whenever I am near my phone with my Fitbit on, they sync and update.  I got special badges for being close to my goal.  It really encouraged me to make sure that I got to my 10,000 steps.  With the app I can log how much water I have drank and how many calories I have eaten and how many I have left.  My husband loves my Fitbit HR and really wants one for himself.  The directions say not to take a shower or go swimming in it.  That is perfectly fine with me.  I just take it off when I take a shower.  I am glad that I went ahead and purchase my Fitbit HR.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

S'more Canvas Camping Tent for 2/3/4 Person, 4 Season Tent, Waterproof, Windproof, and Weather Resistant Glamping Tent, Ideal for Hiking, Backpacking, Family Camping I'd call this a two-person tent. Three might be a little crowded. The peak is not quite six feet tall. The footprint is square. Pitching isn't "instant." It takes a little effort to get it set up. The fabric is very good quality. The seams are tripled and the floor seams are heat sealed. As is often the case with tightly packed items, I couldn't get it all back in the carrying bag like it arrived, but there was enough room in the top straps on the bag to secure the tent pole bag.

Speaking of the poles, they're steel, not aluminum. So, though they're strong, they do add some weight. I'm a little concerned about rust in the long term too. The instructions (they're mostly pictures, and an instruction sheet is actually sewed into the bag) indicate the ends with caps go toward the top. I put them in the other way to keep dirt from getting into the open ends. I may get some more caps so both ends of the poles are covered.

It's not a backpacking tent because of the weight. More like something for car camping. But it's great quality and I'm sure someone with some creativity can really decorate it up for glamping.

text_fidelity_a:
SCHWINN Fitness 430 Elliptical Machine Wow! This elliptical has all the bells and whistles!
I'll go item by item, since there are so many noteworthy features:

**Ease of Assembly: 5 stars
The manual covered everything, and while it took some time to put together this massive box of parts, everything went smoothly and came out perfectly. For you ladies and smaller people, I was able to put it together completely alone (and am female). You probably won't need help--just some podcasts or music to entertain yourself while assembling this amazing machine, and maybe a camera phone to prove you put it together. Takes a few hours, but the feeling of accomplishment is pretty amazing.

**Features and Settings: 4 stars
You can enter user data with age, height, and gender, to get better and more accurate results. Combined with sensors that let you see your heart rate, you can see what sort of activity you are doing (cardiovascular, fat burning, etc.), BUT the heart rate sensor didn't work so well for me. It kept alternating between 120bpm to 60bpm, which made me mistrust the results altogether since this was with a consistent speed, taken short times apart midway through the exercise. Other features worked great though, like different per-programmed settings such as "walk in the park", which was no such thing! It had hills and such, alternating difficulties in a smooth pattern, while some other workouts were even more challenging. The incline can also be easily adjusted to increase or decrease the overall difficulty.

**Extras: 5 stars
There is a USB port to charge your mobile or tablet device!! You can also plug into the auxiliary port to use the speakers and play music--it even comes with the cable needed! The speakers are pretty loud and clear for something like this, so it's a great add-on! There is also a three-setting fan that works well when you get hot.

**Overall workout: 5 stars
The smooth movement that is easy on your knees combined with so many extra features make this an excellent workout tool, with the quality you would expect from a quality gym. I LOVE this machine!
text_fidelity_b: SCHWINN Fitness 430 Elliptical Machine

It’s a simple game and I often find it at local taverns, breweries, etc that have a large outdoor space. It’s also the type of game I find at friend’s houses and so it made sense to get a set of my own, the Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set.

With the American flag design on the two cornhole boards, this set has a patriotic look, which adds to its appeal, since it is certainly better than the plain cornhole boards so common in backyards across America. The boards come complete with bean bags, too, but there is no net to catch the bags, like with some cornhole sets. With this set, the bags will go through the opening and hit the surface beneath, so you need to make sure to place the boards on a reasonably clean surface.

The wood construction of this cornhole set is nice and I like how they attach together with Velcro. There are Velcro strips on the backs of the boards and this makes it easier to carry the boards around. The Velcro keeps them together, so when it comes time to pack up and leave, you almost feel like you’re carrying a single item. They don’t weigh too much either, so it takes little effort to move the boards from place to place.

Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is easy to set up and play straight from the box. The sturdy boards are made to last and the 8 included bean bags weigh 12 oz each, which is heavy enough to make them good for this type of game; less likely to slide past the opening and slide off of the board. The legs fold flat against the backside, so attaching the boards together with the Velcro is easy.

Cornhole is a popular backyard game and since I play it frequently when I go places, I decided it was time to get a game of my own. Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is a very good cornhole game set with a nice design and good durability. It’s a game I recommend for anyone who likes simple, outdoor entertainment for kids and guests.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch (WARNING- This is a long review. I am covering areas about this tent that were a concern to me. If you want a summary, go to the paragraph titled THE BOTTOM LINE)

I wanted to take the time to review this tent. I spent a LOT of hours researching, watching EVERY video and reading every available review I could find out there about this tent to decide which I would get. It was between this tent and [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]]. As it turned out, we had an immediate need for TWO tents, so I got both of them. You can see my review of the [[ASIN:B001TSCF96 Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent]] by clicking the link

WHAT IS THIS TENT LIKE?
One of the things I was concerned about was the thinness of material. We live in a very high elevation and get constant breezes or wind. There were a number of reviews that spoke of their tents snapping or ripping after only a gentle breeze. The fabric is thin, yes. But it does hold up.

Enough people have posted photos, so I won't post one as of yet. The best way to secure this tent is to ALWAYS leave the fly on. An unexpected storm or wind can come up at any time, and I personally feel that the tent is much more stable with the fly on than without. Make sure that you always stake down everything, including ALL of the ropes. That is what keeps the tent stable and secure.

FLOOR
The floor is very nice, and if you use a tarp underneath and take off shoes before entering, it will last quite a while. I also recommend not using chairs with small pointed feet on it either- it will wear out the floor quickly.

WINDOWS
The windows are perfect. They are protected from all but the most severe of rainstorms so you can leave them open if you like. The back window is open at all times, yes, but if staked down, it is not that big of a deal. If we plan to take this on crowded camp sites, I will sew two rings at either back seam and attach a thin fabric when changing. No big deal.

POCKETS AND LANTERN RING
The pockets are nice and in a good space. There is also a ring for hanging a lantern on if you like.

HEIGHT
The height is perfect for us- the tallest is 5 ft 9 inches. Taller people might not like this tent. The screened in porch is a bit narrow for those with long legs. You pretty much need a chair to use it unless you are a kid and don't need to lean back.

SCREENED IN PORCH
I LOVE this thing. I really do. This is my happy place. It is perfect for two camp chairs to look out at night or in the day. The door of the tent can stay open adding to a spacious feel. It does get wet in the rain. I am currently designing a fly to go over the porch and roll up into the tent when not in use. So far I am almost done with the one half of the fly and plan to finish the other half this week if I can. I hope to do that before the tent is taken down.

Without a fly, your stuff will get wet. There is an area that you can sweep the water into when wet, I use a sponge mop to clean it up so it will dry faster. Otherwise it puddles and does take a long time to dry.

POLES
The poles went up well for us, but you just have to take your time when putting up the tent. Do not race through the process, the fabric can rip if you don't.

TENT SPACE
Our biggest concern was ACTUAL usable space for us. We found that putting a queen inflatable double height mattress in there (Coleman) we have plenty of room for two of us. If using an additional single mattress, we can still do it, but it works best with a sleeping bag on the floor and picked up at night if a third person is in there (child).

When using or covering up the porch in rain, the porch makes a great extension for activities, talking, or just sitting and enjoying the view (if not raining). I absolutely love the design of this tent.

LIGHTING
The tent color is half of the beauty of this tent. The light bright colors are cheerful, let in a lot of light, and also keep it from feeling gloomy on rainy days. At night you can see through it, so keep that in mind when you are getting ready at night.

DOES THIS STAY UP IN STORMS?
The big question. I have an answer for you. We purchased this tent the week before Labor Day (US). We put the tent up immediately and treated it with silicone spray. We didn't need to- it is already made from silicone impregnated ripstop nylon. The seams also came pre-treated with silicone on the fly. AMAZING!.

We have had this tent up with daily use since then and it is now October 8,2016. So far it has been through extreme heat, breezes, high winds, thunder storms, all night rains, and heavy rain storms. The tent has stayed up with no observable damage at this point and stayed very dry too.

IMPORTANT POINTS
After reading MANY reviews on this tent, I decided to help it stay up, I would reinforce different areas. Anywhere that there is a plastic hook, I put a piece of garden twist tie into the fabric loop that holds the hook and tied it around the pole to help it absorb any shock of high winds. Any other plastic rings or hooks were reinforced in the same way. I tucked the ends of the twist tie way under so no chance of the fabric blowing into sharp edges and tearing in high winds.

STAKES
I also recommend getting other stakes for the tent. They stay in the ground during storms more easily too. I got [[ASIN:B01IEBKK92 Pack of 16, 7075 Aluminum Outdoors Tent Stakes & Rubber Hammer & Guyline Tensioner with Reflective Pull Cords & Carrying Pouch]] to use in the fly staking process, and used the ones that came with the tent for the actual tent staked to the ground.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Honestly, this is my favorite tent of all time. It is my happy place. I absolutely LOVE the design, set up, colors, and ventilation of this tent. With a mattress, it is still private to lay down with the windows open and you can still look out at the sky and enjoy the scenery. When you are in the tent and want to have breeze, the front door open makes it seem so airy and wonderful. I can not rave about this tent enough. Five weeks of constant use is more than we planned for, but it has held up so far.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED at five stars.

QUESTIONS AND UPDATES
If you have any questions I have not answered, by all means ask. I hope I can be helpful, as I know how it helps me when others do the same. I will update with any more input should I have anything else to share or if there are problems with the tent.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Evanston Screened Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Weatherproof Tent with Roomy Interior Includes Rainfly, Carry Bag, Easy Setup and Screened-in Porch

text_fidelity_a:
Jetboil MightyMo Ultralight and Compact Camping and Backpacking Stove This little camping system works great! Living in California, I've had a series of planned power outages and I had previously and had zero experience cooking with a camp stove. However, once I got over my trepidation, and purchased the branded accessories that go with this kit, I found that this was a very simple cooking solution to use outside during these outages, and it's very lightweight and tiny to store.

I initially purchased a pot support and the jet boil pot, only to find out that I did not actually need the pot support with this model. This is clear on the product page now, but at the time it was not made clear. The jet boil pot did an amazing job of boiling water and cooking things with a high liquid content. It does create a significant hotspot so I found it less good for cooking thicker soups or things like tasty bite lentils. With those things, even with the flame turned down almost as far as it would go, I still got some things sticking to the (I believe anodized aluminum) surface.

I also purchased the nonstick skillet from the brand, because I wanted to be sure that whatever I got was going to work with my stove and be the right size not to tip things over. The skillet also gets some significant hotspots, but by my second morning of cooking eggs, I was doing a much better job of making toast on the skillet and then making eggs to go with and not getting too many brown spots on the eggs.

I purchased my fuel from the hardware store, where it was a much better price than purchasing it online. You do not need to use the branded fuel they sell, which is good because the branded fuel is extremely expensive, as is any fuel when purchased online given the shipping considerations and restrictions.

In terms of setting up this unit, there is a support that holds the gas canister and makes the whole unit much more sturdy, yet the support itself pulls off of the canister and folds down into a tiny little triangle that goes in the palm of your hand. The actual stove also fits in the palm of your hand when all of the pieces are folded down and is this tiny little thing that does not look like it would support a whole cooking pot, but it does. When everything is unfolded perfectly, things do sit steadily on the unit. I found it very easy to twist the unit onto the gas canister, use the little twister to turn the fuel on, and then click the igniter to ignite the fuel and make a fire. Then it was a simple matter from their to cook my food, then turn the little twister again to turn off the fuel entirely. I did store the unit on the gas canister during the duration of the power outage, but disconnected it for storage.

Even as a rookie user of such things, I found it fairly easy to get the hang of doing some good cooking on this thing and after the first power outage had tailored my food supply to things that this unit would cook well – either things that can be fried with the nonstick skillet, or things with a very high liquid content or that you add boiling water too.

Overall I was really pleased with the whole array of accessories that go with this unit and I really appreciate the flux ring cooking pot in particular, which got my boiling water ready for tea in about two minutes. This was very much appreciated in the rain, when I was huddling under the eaves trying not to get wet while making my morning caffeine.
text_fidelity_b: Jetboil MightyMo Ultralight and Compact Camping and Backpacking Stove

AKSOUL Self-Inflating Camping Pad Sleeping Mat - Ultralight Camp Air Mattress Pad Connectable 2 Wide Extra Thick Sleep Pads with Inflatable Pump for 2 Person Durable Compact for Backpacking Hiking My partner and I are elderly, live in hot/humid Georgia, and all the windows in our rental house are painted shut. If we were to experience a blackout here, we would die. After the "What did our grandparents do when they didn't have air conditioning" conversation, we realized that having a few well-ventilated pop-up tent "bedrooms" outside would mimic the screened porches where people used to sleep when it was too hot inside the house. We sleep in separate bedrooms, so two tents will provide ample room for each of us to be comfortable and also not freak out the dogs who insist on sleeping with one or the other of us.

So I ordered the tents and two of these self-inflating double sleeping mats. With waterproof garden tarps I already have under the tents plus a solar panel/generator setup to power laptops, phones, and fans, I think we might be able to survive a blackout. Fortunately, we do have a few shady areas in our back yard where we can pitch our tent rooms. And if we have to evacuate, we can throw our kit into the back of our truck along with our solar oven and kelly kettle.

This sleeping pad is not going to be nearly as comfortable as a real bed, but I think it will be better than nothing. Also, in case of tornado warnings (which we also get), we can use these mats to cover ourselves if we have to hunker down in the bathtub. At our age, regular mattresses are a little hard for us to lift and move. Better to have a plan than to be impotently frightened of climate volatility.
text_fidelity_b: AKSOUL Self-Inflating Camping Pad Sleeping Mat - Ultralight Camp Air Mattress Pad Connectable 2 Wide Extra Thick Sleep Pads with Inflatable Pump for 2 Person Durable Compact for Backpacking Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Gempestoer Mini Personal Water Filter for Hiking Outdoor Mountaineering, Backpacking, Hunting, Field Military Training, Camping, Travel, and Emergency Preparedness (Green) Has anyone tried this? The main filtering aspect seems good, which to me is the most important. But if you are buying this because of the extras, be careful. Here are the details:
--WHISTLE: it works, on or off the filter tube. It twists on/off. Be sure to keep track of it. LOUD.
--COMPASS: Mine doesn't work. It won't adjust to correct direction, or any direction. It doesn't move, period. I had it side by side with one of my other compasses, and it did nothing. Bummer.
--MIRROR: The flip side of the compass has a mirror, for signaling etc. Twist off compass end to access. Very clear, looks good. Slightly smaller than size of a quarter.
--D-ring clip: mediocre, might want something else. It is attached via a basic "key ring", which is then attached through the molded plastic piece on the tube.
--STRAW: this includes a piece of rubber tubing for attaching to filter and using as a straw- either in a bottle, or to add length for being able to access a water source. Will need to figure out way to carry this separately (dont lose it!). Basic tubing size, so should be easy to replace or buy longer tubing.
--FILTER: all points to it working!
OK, back to the filter. I used it on tap water. I suppose I could have wandered out to my creek and grabbed some water. Maybe I will still do that. While our tap water tastes fine, it is noticeably different compared to our on board fridge water filter. I tried this is a mason jar with tap water. I followed directions (blow first to exhaust, then gently draw up water). I could tell how silky smooth the water tasted with no other tastes coming through. I then took a sip of the tap water without the filter straw and could note the "flavor". So this straw is filtering something for sure.

I have lifestraws, and now this. I am a big fan of redundancy and variety, and the saying "two is one and one is none". I keep straws in my "bug out bag", and truck "get home bag". I have even kept on in my purse. Must have for hiking bag. Having viable water source is #1 for me. These things aren't too expensive, so I find it an easy, budget friendly addition to emergency preparedness. The price is spot on for a single straw. Wish the compass worked.
text_fidelity_b: Gempestoer Mini Personal Water Filter for Hiking Outdoor Mountaineering, Backpacking, Hunting, Field Military Training, Camping, Travel, and Emergency Preparedness (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit It’s like magic with a feeling of accomplishment. I don’t think I’ve ever glided before. Stand firm, lean and decide where to wander. It delivers pure delight. That’s the most important element that the Ninebot delivers.

The tech specs are available and don’t need repeating. If you’ve looked this far, you know what all the reviews say. The Ninebot is not the bone breaker ‘hover board’ of past years reputation. It’s a transport device. It’s something different. It’s powerful. It’s solid. The design incorporates a slew of bells and whistles connected and monitored through the smartphone.

Incorporated in the ‘system’ is enforced, demonstrated control teaching. New aspects of transport are unlocked as distance and demonstrated operational progress are accumulated on the Ninebot.

The first climb on board was easy. It is a noticeable step up. You feel the gyros. You sense the control variables. There’s more than I expected. Then I started to overthink. Mistake. Fast get off. The Ninebot is powerful and must be eased into.

I thought about it for a day. It needs respect. To be clear, you can hurt yourself. The step up is significant. The distance down and out of control is adequate for inducing unexpected orthopedic maneuvers.

You think it through again. Helmet? Check. Elbow and wrist support? Check. Watch the videos a few times for subtlety. Try again.

So, I mastered it without injury. I took my time. It’s a bicycle thing. You know it when you know it and you won’t forget.

The tech specs are well defined in the advertised representations. It feels bulkier to carry than the weight might indicat. I am most impressed with the blow-out design, the ‘system integration”, And the power … lots of power. Amazing.
text_fidelity_b: Segway Ninebot S Smart Self-Balancing Electric Scooter, 800W Motor (Ver.S MAX 1000), 13.7 Miles Range(Ver.S MAX 23.6)& 10MPH(Ver.S MAX 12.4), Hoverboard w/t LED Light, Compatible with Gokart Kit

Very glad I didn't - the L size fits just fine, and now that I have one, it's clear the XL would have been too big. That tip from the other reviewers saved me some return postage - thanks!

In terms of the actual glove, it's great. Fits fine, and appears well made. Very secure velcro closure on the wrist.

I use mine for aqua aerobics and to add a "boost" to my swimming workouts. I've used the plastic hand paddle in the past - they are helpful in giving more resistance, but are rather awkward to use. These - if you'll forgive the inevitable pun - fit like a glove and don't get in the way. You can increase or decrease resistance by just expanding or closing your hand.

A word of caution - if you've never used hand paddles or webbed gloves before for exercise, go slow at first. You're putting a lot more strain on your muscles, especially the shoulders. Tempo Expert Fishing Reels, 10 + 1 Ball Bearings from Japan, Max Drags Up to 41 LBs, Light and Smooth Spinning Reel, Magnesium Frame, Gear Ratio from 5.2: 1 to 6.2: 1 I have only recently become familiar with Tempo as a brand in fishing gear and up to this point my experiences with them have been positive. I selected this reel for freshwater use and I chose a smaller size for use on lighter tackle. So far it has been a good reel and it has performed well, but I am a little disappointed in the finish on this one. The QC isn’t quite where it should be and it comes off as a slightly rough test unit instead of a polished retail reel.

I chose the Expert 3000 model as I wanted a smaller reel for catching panfish with lighter tackle. This is a smaller reel than I usually work with, and in use it has proven itself to not be any harder or easier than larger reels for me. It is lighter than usual, though, and that’s a good thing in this case.

It is smooth in the cast and receive which is all I really can ask. There are no hitches in the spinning action, no strange sounds, and the bail flips properly. The drag is easy to set and works well too. The greatest strength of this reel is actually the zero-reverse clutch - this reel gives exactly nothing when the zero reverse clutch is engaged. Many reels allow for a tiny amount of reverse play, but this one does not.

Operationally, this reel is fine and I have no complaints at all. Where I have an issue with this reel is in the fit and finish. The reel body is put together with star screws, and some of these protrude slightly and are rough to the touch. The more serious issue is the spool, though, which has sharp edges on the parallel cuts, sharp enough to feel easily and could under the right circumstances damage line if there is a backlash or rat’s nest. Neither of these issues are enough to make this reel unusable, but at the price point the reel should be pretty close to perfect.

I do like this reel and I will get good service out of it. It works very well and it is lightweight, perfect for the lake where I plan to use it. My main reservation is just in the finish, where it seems some attention to detail is lacking.
text_fidelity_b: Tempo Expert Fishing Reels, 10 + 1 Ball Bearings from Japan, Max Drags Up to 41 LBs, Light and Smooth Spinning Reel, Magnesium Frame, Gear Ratio from 5.2: 1 to 6.2: 1

text_fidelity_a:
KENAI 65 Cooler | 65 qt Ice Chest Durable Rotomolded Insulated | Made in USA | Warranty for Life | for Beach Boat Camping Fishing Hunting | K65 UPDATE AFTER VACATION;
the best thing about this cooler for longer trips, its dry ice ready. We spent 15$ on dry ice, used the divider (frozen) and our ice didnt start to melt until day 6 on the way home. This cooler worked as well as the Yeti for 3x less money. I'm so happy and proud of my cooler I use it almost everyday. Our beach trip was a total success and we saved 6$ a day on ice at the minimum. Perfect cooler for everyday use, beach, river, lake and just about any time you need. Plenty of room and easy to clean. A must buy

Update, 1st use breakdown.

Did NOT precool cooler, Used Grizzly Brand ice divider (owns Kenia coolers), and my cans were pre chilled in fridge.
I only used 1 half of my cooler using the frozen divider. The other half stayed empty.

10lbs ice 1st day ( rd side ice machine which isnt the best ice and melts quick) after 36 hrs I only had around 2 cups of water because the divider was refreezing the water as it melted against the divider and along the bottom of cooler.
Day 3 I added 20lbs of frozen ice. Still only half of cooler. Didnt have but a quart or so of melt off by this point and divider was half melted. The ice last 2 more days before I drained 1.25 to 1.5 gallons of water from cooler and had maybe 7 lbs of lightly frozen ice left.

This cooler is awesome from my use and my experience with using it. Today I've added 20lbs of ice NO divider and using entire cooler and I still only have a cup of water. Temp is 80 degrees constantly and 15 hrs have gone by already. This is still the rd side machine ice, as I said before in a normal cooler 20lbs will melt within 20 hrs for sure by next morning it's all water. With the Kenia cooler I have easily doubled my ice time if not almost tripling it. And I'm not freezing the ice in a freezer before use. If you freeze this crap ice before use, it can last 4 or so days. If u freeze ice in deep freezer I'm sure it will last even longer because of the - temps with deep freezer.

Well worth the money spent and saved vs a 600$ equivalent yeti. This cooler will pay for it self over 40 total days, 5$ or more per bag ice, 1 bag per day 200$... paid for that quick. At least with my old coolers this is what I was having to do, either 6$ bag ice from store or 2 rd side bags @4$ per day. Every day and during our Southern 100 degree days I was having to do this twice a day. So by far this cooler out last most on market.

Now I added 20 lbs of frozen freezer ice to that 10lbs, didnt drain the water. The ice lasted 4 days. I hope this helps someone make the right choice for the money.
We have a beach trip planned in few months and another updated test results will come after that trip. That test will be outside in middle summer outside 16+ hrs a day in direct sunlight. Will update after words to tell the world.

Look 5 stars even though ITS LOOKS TO BE USED!!
yes it is scratched on top and scuffed on side and bottom and it does not smell like a factory cooler smells when purchased. With the way its wrapped and boxed this shouldnt happen if it was brand new. I could be wrong and issues arise from warehouse worshipping problems. But it seems to be a returned item that has been used at least once.

Overall this cooler is huge, thick, and very sturdy! Cheaper by almost 70% from yeti brand. I'm very pleased with purchase.
The color is absolutely vibrant and eye catching. I love the stapdown handles and the thick rubber feet on bottom.
The inside is just amazing you can tell it will hold heat or cold very easily.

I wish there were more accessories available with the 65 quart coolers.. that's my only big issue besides the used look.
I bought a rack from yeti hoping to bend it the .1 inch to fit (judging by measurements provide by companies). I have also bought the 5lbs freezer divider so we can keep usable ice seperate from used ice with the dry ice.

Camping trip in next few weeks will give a good idea of how well this cooler cools. Will update at that time and let everyone know how this cooler works in real world settings.

I have not been paid for ANY review I've ever left. (I wish I did though) This is, as always, just my opinion through my eyes to help others.
If you find this review helpful, please vote, so Amazonian browsers can better learn, research and understand how products work for them.!. Thank you and Happy Buying
text_fidelity_b: KENAI 65 Cooler | 65 qt Ice Chest Durable Rotomolded Insulated | Made in USA | Warranty for Life | for Beach Boat Camping Fishing Hunting | K65

CITYSPORTS Treadmills for Home, Under Desk Treadmill Walking Pad with Audio Speakers, Slim & Portable Remote Dual LED Display, Office Home I went from a fairly active job to a desk job; after a week, my calves were tight and sore so I didn't hesitate to purchase this desk treadmill when it came up on the deal of the day list. The reviews were awesome for it too, and I have to agree!

It's easy to move on your own, easy to operate, and quiet. I don't use the bluetooth feature and I don't "run" on it (seeing as how it only gets up to 3.8 mph!) :) Ultimately, I walk on it for the 99 minutes it allows before cutting off at about 2.0 mph while working at my computer; anywhere around this speed is perfect for me to feel comfortable without fear of falling off as I clack away at my keyboard. At 99 minutes, it automatically turns off which is a great reminder for me to take a break and then I rinse and repeat once or twice more throughout the day.

There's a little flap on the top left to add lubricating oil and that was easy too (just fill to the top! Which - lubricating oil was included). My fiance was afraid it would leave stains on the carpet but nope!

The shipping and delivery was great - quick and fast, and I've had it for about two months now. I love it so far and am happy for the purchase.

If you're looking for something with incline and high speeds for challenging runs and workout, this is not for you. If you're looking for something slow, steady, quiet, but comfortable and easy to use (especially with remote), this is your treadmill! Although - don't purchase the assembly services Amazon tries to sell you. It literally is a matter of removing it from the box, removing any plastic wrapping, placing it where you want it, plug it in, flip the power switch, turn treadmill/belt on with remote, and increase/decrease speed. It really should say no assembly required! :)

I've also crochet, read, watch TV and listened to music/podcasts (of course) and other activities while just casually walking. With the winter months and snow, it's perfect for making up the missed outdoor physical activities and I love that I can multitask!

text_fidelity_a:
Abom 5 in 1 Multicolor Tactical Flashlight Kit, White Red Green Blue Light Torch with Memory Zoomable for Hunting, Fishing, Night Vision, Include Battery, Charger, Traffic Signal Wand Overall, this is a very good flashlight for the price. The build quality is quite good, with an all-metal case, solid tactile feedback on the power button and decent threading. It takes either 3AA (adapter included) or an 18650. While it will work with the AA's, you really need to use an 18650 to get the most out of it. It works well with both flat and button top 18650's. While an adapter is included to prevent battery rattle, the contact springs are strong enough to hold the cell without any rattling. I've tried it with cells from Sanyo, Panasonic, LG and Sony without an issue.

The beam can be focused by sliding the hood. The sliding motion is fairly smooth. Bean strength is excellent considering the price point for this flashlight.

When the flashlight is on, a light press on the power button will cycle it through it's modes (regular, blue, red and green). It's a nice feature to have and sets this apart from other inexpensive single 18650 flashlights. However, it also causes a major irritation -- if you're in regular light mode and turn it off, when you turn it back on it will be in blue mode. You then have to cycle through red and green modes to go back to regular mode. Very annoying -- there should be a separate button (perhaps on the housing) for color, and let the power button be just for power.

That annoyance aside, no complaints. It provides a lot of functionality and value for the price. Four stars overall given the need to cycle through the light modes each time, but otherwise it's a 5-star flashlight for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Abom 5 in 1 Multicolor Tactical Flashlight Kit, White Red Green Blue Light Torch with Memory Zoomable for Hunting, Fishing, Night Vision, Include Battery, Charger, Traffic Signal Wand

I'm going to keep the #1, but I'm also ordering a CoC Trainer, which has a 100lb pull, so I can work up to it. That's what I'd recommend for anyone who is fit but just starting grip training in earnest.

EDIT: Okay, so I ordered the Training model and used that for a few weeks. I could close that one with some effort, and quickly built my way up to sets of twelve. Now I can do sets of about three on the #1. Once I can hit sets of about twenty on this one, I'll move up.

text_fidelity_a:
Body Bar Power & Grace DVD This workout uses both a body bar and the gliding disks. Instructor Mindy Mylrea is joined by Keli Roberts, who modifies some of the exercises, and Violet Zaki, who increases the intensity.

Mylrea starts with a long (about 7 minutes) warm-up. During the warm-up, you are just holding the body bar and not really using it for resistance. In addition, she does not step on the disks until about halfway through the warm-up; at that time, she incorporates added moves such as twists plus side and back lunges.

For the standing portion of the workout, Mylrea takes greater advantage of the body bar. The option is often to hold the bar at the chest, on the shoulders, or overhead while performing classic strength moves such as side and front lunges, curtsey lunges, and deadlifts. The standing segment ends with push-up/plank work with the feet on the disks.

The floor work is shorter (18 minutes), but it continues to focus on the lower body with bridges and other moves targeting the hamstrings. Mylrea also includes abs work and a nice floor stretch (6 minutes), bringing in the entire workout right around 54 minutes.

I really enjoy Mylrea's original Gliding set, as I like mixing and matching from the 3 workouts on that DVD. For some reason, this workout didn't click as well with me, even though there aren't any major problems with the workout itself. One issue is that I do not have a body bar; substituting an unweighted stick and dumbbells worked okay, but this took some fun out of the workout. I also think that I have moved away from these type of cardio/strength circuit workouts now that I have discovered kettlebells.

For those who own both a body bar and gliding disks, however, I would recommend this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: Body Bar Power & Grace DVD

text_fidelity_a:
Eureka! Solitaire AL 1 Person, 3 Season, Camping and Backpacking Tent This Eureka Solitaire should be considered more as a bivy than a tent. I suppose it is more a bivy/tent hybrid. Being an inbetween, it is not super light, but is not super heavy either. Weight on this is 3 lbs, 2 oz. That is with poles, stakes, guy lines, and carry bag. So the tent is not an ultralight, especially for the size of this thing.
Pros:
1. Packs down small and does not take up much room in a backpack.
2. Fairly light
3. Fly can be rolled up to allow for maximum airflow when the weather permits.
Cons:
1. Not free standing. Must be staked down.
2. Fly is not removable.
3. No vestibule.
4. Must crawl in/out from the front. Can be hard to keep from getting wet/dirty if there was a storm/rain the night before.

Overall, if you are looking for a bivy style tent, this probably is what you want. Unless you want an ultra-light, which this is not.
I personally would not recommend this style of tent. But, if you are looking for a nicely built bivy tent, this is probably it, if you do not mind the weight.
Would be really good for motorcycle or bike camping. Not really for backpacking, as the weight is comparable to a good 2 person tent!
If I were going to carry a 3lb+ tent, I would get one with enough room to sit up in and that has a vestibule. Plenty of those tents out there in the 3lb range.
text_fidelity_b: Eureka! Solitaire AL 1 Person, 3 Season, Camping and Backpacking Tent

MSR changed the caps or cap supplier and the new caps are defective. I screwed on one of the caps from a Dromedary Lite I purchased 15 years ago, and it would not leak. The old caps, which have been supplied as recently as a year ago, have "wash and dry after each use" molded on them. The new caps do not and are thicker on the edges and have sharper grip teeth. Fix the caps and I will change the rating. In the mean time, I will probably have to buy Nalgene caps or something to replace the junk MSR is selling.

The design is top-notch. The fact that the caps are interchangeable with Nalgene, fit water filters, and the nylon bags are tougher than plastic are all a testament to the fact these bags can be the best. They're the only bag I trust to fill with hot water and slip in my sleeping bag in the winter. They're awesome, 5-star products if they're made correctly.

I have a hydromedary kit I used on the bigger bags (6L) for at least 15 years. I replaced the hose before with regular vinyl tubing from the hardware store. The tubing on this hydromedary is smaller in diameter but still looks like standard vinyl tubing and could easily be replaced.

WAAO Hand Grip Strengthener Workout, Hand Exerciser, Strength Trainer, Adjustable Resistance Range 22-88 Lbs, Non-Slip Gripper, Great for Athletes Pianists Kids & Hand Rehabilitation Exercising I've never had great hand strength and thought this device might help. The bright blue handles are easy to hold. There is a black knob which turns to adjust the resistance. Resistance ranges from 22-88 lbs. Unfortunately there are no directions or training suggestions included. I started using the lowest setting. To start, hold the strengthener in the palm of your hand. Wrap your fingertips around one of the handles so that it rests in the middle of your fingers. Your fingertips should cover it while the other handle is positioned against the lower part of your palm.Squeeze the handles together while you exhale and inhale as you slowly return to the starting position. I try to do a set of six to eight repetitions. try to keep the rest of your body still while performing. I stay at a resistance until it becomes easy and then I move up. My mother uses this device also. Since having a stroke, her hands are very weak and her grip strength is minimal. She started with one to two repetitions and is slowly gaining strength and endurance. It certainly performs well, seems to be well made and should last.

I received a complimentary/discounted product for testing and review.
text_fidelity_b: WAAO Hand Grip Strengthener Workout, Hand Exerciser, Strength Trainer, Adjustable Resistance Range 22-88 Lbs, Non-Slip Gripper, Great for Athletes Pianists Kids & Hand Rehabilitation Exercising

I did way too much research and finally settled on this one. Priorities were weight limits, size, durability, and bounce. The trampoline was easy to install, liked that the spring pull tool is included and is needed. 2 Adults about 40 minutes. The Acon name on the mat points up (goofed on this so had to flip)
I went with the premium enclosure, inside of springs vs outside. It gives a feeling of less bounce area or hang out area but I figured less wear on the spring pad. Also, maybe a bit more safe since they can only land on the bounce mat. I lost the instructions right away but was able to install it correctly after a bit of trial and error (found them as I was putting my tools away..grr ) Had I had the instructions, this would of taken me about 1.5 hours (for enclosure only), 30 minutes was weaving the enclosure on and another 15 minutes finding the right socket to fit on my drill (metric but standard worked).
Kids have been jumping on it with all the neighborhood kids. A little less bouncy than our 14 year old trampoline but once the springs get broken in should be a great bounce.
Pros- Huge, looks very safe, less pricey than other good quality trampolines, includes what is needed, each piece is heavy and heavy duty. Can hold hundreds of pounds.
Cons- The Premium netting takes 2 persons to put up because of the upper ring. Because of the upper netting frame, looks like it will very timely and hard to take down for snowy winters.

Heat Socks for Women Men with 5000mAh Power Bank, 2 Pairs Rechargeable Electic Heated Socks with 4 Levels Heating Socks, Winter Warm Socks for Outdoor/Sports/Huting/Fishing/Camping TL;DR - these are really really nice heated socks.
I don't live in a cold climate, but I have poor circulation and my feet get cold day, and these are enough on low to take the chill off, and I found medium-low to be great for therapeutic heat.
The socks are knee high and fit a size 12 foot and medium calves with a bit of room to spare. The material is very soft and comfortable and I didn't get any binding, I also noticed less bunching up in the foot area. The heat is indeed all over and feels nicely even. Including a second pair of just socks was really smart. Aside from the inevitable wet foot, being able to charge while wearing makes it more practical to run 2 sets of socks with 1 set of batteries.
I really like the design for the battery packs, having a small button on the battery is a lot less likely to be accidentally pushed than the typical big rubber button on the outside. Battery info is also well displayed and simple - blue is temp and green is battery life.
I especially like that these are charged with standard USB-C so that I don't need to worry about having a special adapter with me. The batteries also seem to support pass through charging, so you can run cords from battery packs to get more use in one outing while also charging up the packs. Starting from full and running half the time on low and half on medium-low, I got about 9hrs before they died.
FYI - most heated socks I've seen on Amazon are rated about 7.4V, whereas these are rated like battery packs (3.7V), so the amperage ratings can seem like more than it is - 5Ah (5000mAh) at 3.7V is 18.5Wh; whereas the average 7.4V battery is around 2.5Ah (2500mAh) which is also 18.5Wh. So despite the much higher mAh rating, these have no more energy than most any other heated sock.
text_fidelity_b: Heat Socks for Women Men with 5000mAh Power Bank, 2 Pairs Rechargeable Electic Heated Socks with 4 Levels Heating Socks, Winter Warm Socks for Outdoor/Sports/Huting/Fishing/Camping

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds This tent was packaged well. Easy to follow directions and was very simple to set up. I am an Eagle Scout and have been camping for over 35 years so the tent was pretty intuitive to set up. It says "Weathertec - guarenteed to keep you dry" on the outside. I read everything for sealing instructions prior to taking this to the woods. No requirements for sealing included and in fact it said all seams taped. I felt pretty confident. The weekend was calling for temps in the 50's and rain (not hard... just drizzle). I opened and tested the setup prior to camp. It was easy and seemed large enough. I took it out and had it set in approximately 30 seconds. The tent was spacious for two 6'2 guys and gear (cots) sleeping gear small packs and room to spare. It was shorter than expected and a bit smaller than I hoped... topping off about 5'5" at a guess and very tight with a cot (it touched the wall on both ends). The worst was the rain. It held up well to the first 1/2 hour or so but soon it was leaking. By 2am... it was damp... by morning there was about a cup of water in the floor. And the walls were soaked. The bathtub floor retained all the water. It leaked very badly. From seemingly every pore. The second night I spent alone in the dead center. Sleeping bag was soaked the tent was soaked and everything I had was damp even though it was in a chair or on a cot. It took over a day to dry the tent out to ship it back. All this from a light drizzle. Less than 1/2 inch of rain over two days. The firewood on the ground outside was dryer than the personals in my tent. On a scale of 1-10 Ease of set up 10, keeping out bugs 10, big windows 10... this could be a great shelter on a clear day but waterproof 1.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds

Cyfie Fishing Tool Kit Stainless Steel Pliers, Saltwater Resistant Lip Gripper Multitool for Angler, Father, Men, Boyfriend… This kit is actually better quality than I thought it would be. I really just needed the pliers and lip gripper, but since this was all in a package, I decided to get the whole kit.
It comes with the pliers, a gripper, a clipper/knot tool, a zinger, a folding net and a pair of gloves, so it's a nice package and would be good as a gift.
The folding net is pretty sturdy and folds together easily. It is about 3 feet from the tip of the net to the end of the handle when extended. The net is plascic or soft rubber and that is good for not harming the fish. The net itself is 15 inches wide at the top and about 6 inches wide at the bottom and is 15 inches from front to back. It would be good for panfish, bass or even trout. It has a clip on the handle so you can put it on your belt, but I'm not sure how that would work out. In any event, it's a nice net.
The pliers are very good, they have a sheath and a wrist strap and the lip grabber is also good. The clipper and knot tool are also well made and the zinger is a nice one that extends out about 12-15 inches. it has a carabiner type thing that you can use to attach to a belt loop.
It also comes with a pair of gloves with the thumb and two finger ends cut out. They are lightweight and seem to be ok, although I've never seen fishing gloves with the fingers cut out.
All in all, it's a nice kit and most likely was designed for bass and panfish. I'll use the lip grabber and pliers when I go to Canada fishing for large northern, but the rest of it I'll keep for fishing in the local ponds.
text_fidelity_b: Cyfie Fishing Tool Kit Stainless Steel Pliers, Saltwater Resistant Lip Gripper Multitool for Angler, Father, Men, Boyfriend…

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) Purchased this for my wife for Christmas, but I have given it to her early because she is concerned about heart rate and sleeping patterns.This review is a bit premature in light of the fact that I have yet to get any feedback from her on things life comfort and accuracy. But I thought I would try to help out others who are considering purchase of this item.

1. So far, out of the box it seems to be working properly.
2. There is no manual with the item. I found one on the Amazon site as part of the item description. If you wish to print the manual, the needed part is 19 pp.
3. You have the choice of using the fitbit with a smartphone or a puter. My wife is using it with her phone, which makes it highly portable with stats available on the phone app.
4. The battery in the unit is apparently NOT replaceable -- at least the manual offers no info on this point.
5. With normal use, the batt charge will last for 5 days. It can be recharged only one way, via USB port on a puter. There is no power cord, other than the USB cord that comes with the unit. I charged it and it took about an hour to reach full charge.
6. Now this is important if you don't want to wind up torturing yourself, as happened to me: REMOVE the piece of plastic that covers the watch crystal on the fitbit. The plastic piece is black and has a useless number on it. When you do the phone setup, the pairing with bluetooth will provide you with a 4-digit code. You cannot see the code unless you remove that piece of plastic protector.

Once my wife lets me know how the unit is doing, I will update this review with additional info. I hope you find this preliminary info helpful!

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03 I love the app. It’s super user-friendly, and offers clear menus with your collected info, with options to connect with social media, plot running trails, and find popular places to walk/jog. If I were reviewing this solely on the app, this product would easily earn five stars,

BUT....

The data is 100% off. This is probably the most inaccurate fitness tracker I’ve used so far, both for step counts and sleep tracking. I used it for a little over a week to see if it could “learn”, or if different activities tracked more accurately, and it was pretty inconsistent.

Steps: I set a goal of 7,000 steps, which with my other trackers was a High goal. I could teach/take 3 hours of cardio-heavy dance and have regular activities other than that like cleaning up the house, doing office stuff, checking mail, etc, and I would *sometimes* get to 7,000. That’s Three Hours of cardio. Meanwhile, the last week has been full of house renovating, but that mostly consisted of staying in one place and repairing things, organizing things, and making runs to the hardware store. It did NOT consist of many steps or a bunch of walking. Even so, it said I made it to something around 9,000 steps. There is No Way I took that many steps. If I had to guess, I *maybe* made it to 5k. All week has been the same, with Very exaggerated counts.

Sleep: fail. More than half the nights, it showed no data at all and advised me to wear the band. I have literally not removed this thing even once in over a week, not even for showering. Other nights, it said I slept 8.5 hours, when I know I slept under four. I remembered the time I turned everything off and closed my eyes it was around 4am. I woke up around 8am. The phone said I was asleep by 11:30ish. Another night, it said I slept 10 hours, from 8pm-6-am. I can’t think of a time in the last decade that I’ve gone to bed at 8. I am practically a vampire. And that was on a day I finally got to sleep in, so I woke up at around 11. When I tried editing the data in hopes of teaching it, the system was buggy. I saved and exited the screen, and it went right back to the incorrect stuff. This would happen a few times, and in the end, I was only able to correct one of the nights successfully. I don’t have the energy to keep trying. Maybe it will get better, maybe not, but I’m not doing extra data entry work for this.

So all in all, I can’t recommend this product. The data is consistently wrong, which makes it practically impossible to assess what you’re doing or not doing.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03

CamelBak Skyline LR 10 Bike Hydration Backpack - Crux Lumbar Reservoir - 100 oz My daughter and I like to ride our bikes. We also like to go for long walks. Having this hydrating pack was a fabulous opportunity because carrying water is a pain for both of us. This makes it a whole new experience.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
COMPARTMENTS
This has a variety of compartments in it. There is the one for water which has room for storing some simple clothing items like a windbreaker or thin layer of clothing. IT has two side compartments which fit money, phones, keys, etc. Also it will fit a small tool kit for the bike. There is the top compartment which is small but will fit mace, or other small items you might need on your ride.

STRAPS
The straps are really comfortable, not at all binding and are perfect for riding. There are a few spots to put some small items on through loops if you need to. There is a front strap that holds them together too. Again perfect.

WATER DISPENSING
This holds a great amount of water. Despite being heavy, this is very well centered. The water dispensing tube has a double system. First you flip the lever to seal it and lock it shut, then you have the silicone closure which you have to kind of press open with your teeth and suck on with your mouth. The water comes out very easily.

MAGNETIC CLOSURE
The magnetic closure on this hydrating pack is slid out while you ride to free up the tube, and then when you put it back, the magnet pulls it into place so it is easy to use while riding.

ANY PROBLEMS OR LEAKING?
There were no instructions with this and the lever that is flipped is a pain to use while riding. I have tried it with the lever in an open position and so far not leaking, but I am not sure how long that will last.

BACK PADDING
This is fabulous. It has a tunnel in it which allows for the back to stay cooler. It really does provide some nice airflow.

COMFORT
This is VERY comfortable to wear. It is almost as if it is not on, it is so well centered on the back.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hydration pack is fantastic. It is easy to wear and use (once the lever is opened), has a nice magnet to keep it in place, and is centered beautifully with great airflow to the back.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This does not have tons of storage room on it, but enough for essentials. It is a very handy item and we have used it a lot so far and will continue to do so. HIGHLY recommended.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Skyline LR 10 Bike Hydration Backpack - Crux Lumbar Reservoir - 100 oz

FILA Accessories Hand Therapy Kit - Hand Strengthener, Wrist Strengthener Kit - 2-Inch Balls with 2 Resistance Levels (Soft/Medium and Medium/Firm) - Includes Guide I work a lot with my hands. I have noticed while knitting lately that I could use some exercise to keep my hands and wrists from getting sore, so I thought I would try these out.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These two balls that come in this kit are two different types. One is very soft and the other is a little harder to press. The lime one is the softer one that you begin with. This comes with a sheet that has photos and descriptions of different exercises to do. I have to say that the cautions of catching breath and heart problems made me chuckle.

HOW DO THESE WORK?
I have been using the softer version at first doing the exercises daily and did notice after a week that my hands were not hurting as much when I was knitting. I just changed to the stiffer one and it is more challenging, but it feels nice on the hands, forearms and wrists.

VIDEOS?
I did not find any videos on these, but if I do, I will update.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For strengthening hands, fingers, and forearms, this is a great simple kit. Exercises are easy to follow with photos and descriptions. I did notice some relief after just a week.

MY RATING
This is a nice kit. It helps with knitting and other hands on activities. I am giving this five stars as it is easy to store- not too big- and easy to use too.

Joby Gorillatorch Blade Tactical Flashlight I was highly impressed with this flashlight. It is a nice, clean design, and the adjustable tripod allows you to put the light right where you need it, especially in tight places such as in the interior of a computer. The rear switch is perfect for carrying the light in your fist and working with your thumb. A real plus: it has flat sides so when you put it down it does not roll away!

The light itself is very bright (I almost want to advise "Do not look into light with remaining eyeball"), especially on the highest setting. You can adjust the aperture for a wide or a narrow beam. We have inadequate lighting in our back yard, which extends back at least 15 yards (probably more), and using this flashlight in almost total darkness I could see the details of the trees and back fence while walking our dog.

USB charging is very convenient, since it is now such a universal technology. When plugged in to charge, the unit glows blue until done, so it's very easy to know when its finished. This is an excellent piece of equipment for use in an emergency kit or just for plain everyday use.

Downsides: the rear cover over the charging port and the switch seem flimsy, and there's no way to change out the battery that I can find (nor is it mentioned in the manual). However, I would still highly recommend this product.
text_fidelity_b: Joby Gorillatorch Blade Tactical Flashlight

text_fidelity_a:
KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light This is a bike light that techies might like more than most bicyclists. The light is modular and you can buy an extra mount for another bike, a spare battery pack or even a higher powered light head if you want. The light is also programmable; you can plug it into your computer via USB and customize the lighting modes or change which modes are available. Are these useful features or gimmicks? You have to decide.

Regarding the main feature of this light, it works very well. The full power 600L mode is very bright in the center and the beam has some width so you can see the sides of the road. The 600L mode gave me about 2 hours of use, which is great for a dark commute. Lower power modes gave me much longer burn times. The price for this light is not bad for the performance (brightness and run time). Some people are turned off by all the gimmick features, but I don't think those add much to the price at all.

I like the twist to activate feature of this light. Most lights use push buttons that can be hard to press when your fingers or wet or cold or when you are wearing gloves. Twist and hold to turn the light on and it returns to your previous mode. Twist quickly to cycle through the modes.

My only real complaint about this light is the handlebar clamp. It is thin plastic. It seems sturdy and replacements are available. However, it has a hinged design with just one small bolt and I could not tighten it enough to keep it rock solid steady when I was riding. That's not a huge problem for a light (as opposed to a camera), but I think this problem could be solved with a better clamp (like the metal 2-bolt clamps that you can buy for GoPro cameras).

Like all Knog products, this light is sleek and stylish. The all metal body looks and feels nice and will hopefully be durable.
text_fidelity_b: KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light

text_fidelity_a:
YOGABODY Yoga Trapeze Pro – Yoga Inversion Swing with Free Video Series and Pose Chart, Purple Updating this review after more than 5 years. I still have this, it’s held up quite well, and I definitely still use it. There is definitely a learning curve, and I still have trouble getting it in just the right spot to hand upside down without the fabric digging into me. BUT, once I AM n the right spot, I can hang there for 5-10 minutes and the benefits are great. I am overweight (but working on it!) and that definitely adds to the difficulty. There are so many other things that can be done with this prop though… my son was in a near fatal car accident, had many surgeries, and this device helped him immensely during his physical therapy. I’m leaving the negative stuff I wrote below just to be fully transparent. I really WAS disappointed at first, but I love it now
——————————————————
I am sad to be writing a negative review. I wanted one of these things for years! (A yoga swing, not necessarily this brand.) I bought this primarily for inverted poses to help with back pain. The cloth digs into my lower back and upper thighs terribly when I hang upside down... to the point of actual pain. I followed installation instructions; stood with my arms out, bent them up in a 90° angle and then installed the hardware to hang it from on the ceiling. I bought the suggested hardware. It feels as if this is too far apart, and I read installation instructions for another company's yoga swing which said to install the hardware no more and no less than 16" apart. Maybe this would help? I've tried bunching up the fabric and rearranging it in all different ways. If anyone has a suggestion I would be most grateful. For the price I paid (and when similar products cost HALF what this one does) I WANT to be happy with it. For now, I am extremely disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: YOGABODY Yoga Trapeze Pro – Yoga Inversion Swing with Free Video Series and Pose Chart, Purple
